text:
maria: Quick sync — we need to lock the KV/prefix cache telemetry contract this week so console + routing can build the dashboard and quota signals. Key consumers: routing policies (fallbacks), quota scoring, console heatmaps. Core metrics requested: per-workload hit rate, evictions (count + reason), prefix-length reuse distribution, and warm-start / cold-start counts. Who can confirm feasibility from runtime?

alex: I can produce counters + histograms from the runtime. Plan: counters for hits/misses/evictions, labelled by model, route, workload. Histogram for prefix reuse (bucketed: 1,2,4,8,16,32+). Concern: label cardinality if we add tenant or full route path.

jia: Cardinality is the main cost for infra. Suggest labels: model, route_id, workload_id. Do NOT attach full tenant id by default — only for enterprise telemetry with opt-in. Also add seq_len_bucket to help correlate with cache effectiveness.

sam: Retention note from infra: raw high-cardinality TS are expensive. Proposal: 1m granularity, 7d full retention, 30d aggregated rollups (hourly). Additionally sample 0.5% of requests that include full key traces (for debugging evictions).

alex: Agree. We'll also emit eviction_reason as a label with low cardinality (eg: capacity, ttl_expired, explicit_invalidate, eviction_policy) and an evictions_total counter with that label. Need a tiny proto change to the metrics envelope to include workload_id and prefix_len bucket. Draft proto below: \n\n```proto\nmessage KVCacheMetrics {\n  string workload_id = 1;\n  string model = 2;\n  string route_id = 3;\n  uint64 hits = 4;\n  uint64 misses = 5;\n  uint64 evictions = 6;\n  map<string,uint64> evict_reasons = 7;\n  Histogram prefix_reuse = 8; // buckets: 1,2,4,8,16,32+\n  uint64 warm_starts = 9;\n  uint64 cold_starts = 10;\n}\n```\n
jia: Looks good. One API debate: should runtime emit "effective_hit_rate" gauge or should console compute it from hits/misses? My vote: compute on the ingest side for simpler downstream joins (but tag as derived).

alex: Runtime can emit derived gauges at 1m cadence so dashboards don't have to compute across rollups. We'll prefix derived metrics with "derived_". E.g. derived_kv_hit_rate{workload_id,model,route_id}.

maria: UX asks: console needs a per-route heatmap (time x prefix-length reuse), a per-workload trend (hit rate, evictions), and an "estimated cost impact" card that shows tokens saved if hit rate improves. Also routing wants thresholds: define cold/warm/hot buckets so the policy can fallback when workload is cold. Propose thresholds: hot >= 0.8, warm >= 0.5, cold < 0.5. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

sam: Those thresholds seem fine to start. We'll also need an alert when evictions spike > 3x baseline or when overall hit rate drops > 15% in 15m window.

aj: (typo) jia: small ask — add a sample key tracer that includes the actual prefix and chosen cache key (sanitized) for debugging. These should be scrubbed and only sampled at low rate.

alex: Will add a sampled "kv_key_trace" event at 0.5% with fields: workload_id, model, prefix_len, sanitized_key_hash, eviction_reason (if any).

maria: One internal API question: telemetry vs control-plane config. We need the runtime to emit workload_id based on route config. @eng-platform owns mapping route -> workload. Alex, do you need a config endpoint or will the runtime read route metadata?

alex: Runtime already reads route metadata from local config. I just need the canonical workload_id field in the route manifest. I'll open a tiny schema PR.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: PR opened by @alex for metrics proto + sample exporter: https://git.internal/repo/PR/4123 :rocket:

maria: Action items:
- alex: PR for proto + exporter (open) — add derived_kv_hit_rate at 1m cadence (owner: alex)
- sam: cost estimate for retaining these series at proposed retention (owner: sam)
- jia: dashboard mockups: heatmap + per-workload cards + threshold UI (owner: jia)
- maria: write routing policy doc that references thresholds and fallback logic (owner: maria)

maria: Let's reconvene Thurs 10am to sign off. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
